admin_cluster_membership.description:
The admin cluster this VMware User Cluster belongs to.
This is the full resource name of the admin cluster's hub membership.
In the future, references to other resource types might be allowed if
admin clusters are modeled as their own resources.
admin_cluster_membership.rationale: admin cluster membership is not sensitive enough for policy compliance

annotations.description:
Annotations on the VMware User Cluster.
This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations.
The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k.
Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required),
separated by a slash (/).
Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: annotations do not impact the security of the service

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

anti_affinity_groups.description:
AAGConfig specifies whether to spread VMware User Cluster nodes across at
least three physical hosts in the datacenter.

anti_affinity_groups.aag_config_disabled.description:
Spread nodes across at least three physical hosts (requires at least three
hosts).
Enabled by default.
anti_affinity_groups.aag_config_disabled.rationale: aag_config_disabled does not impact the security of the service

authorization.description: RBAC policy that will be applied and managed by GKE On-Prem.

authorization.admin_users.description:
Users that will be granted the cluster-admin role on the cluster, providing
full access to the cluster.

authorization.admin_users.username.description: The name of the user, e.g. 'my-gcp-id@gmail.com'.
authorization.admin_users.username.rationale: Names a principal granted cluster admin access. As an access-granting principal it is a valid policy target: enforce against public/wildcard principals so admin access is never granted broadly; the policy must not pin specific user identities.

control_plane_node.replicas.description:

load_balancer.metal_lb_config.description: Configuration for MetalLB typed load balancers.

load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.description:
AddressPools is a list of non-overlapping IP pools used by load balancer
typed services. All addresses must be routable to load balancer nodes.
IngressVIP must be included in the pools.

The addresses that are part of this pool. Each address
must be either in the CIDR form (1.2.3.0/24) or range
form (1.2.3.1-1.2.3.5).
load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.rationale: addresses is not security impactful enough to warrant policy compliance

load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.description:
If true, avoid using IPs ending in .0 or .255.
This avoids buggy consumer devices mistakenly dropping IPv4 traffic for
those special IP addresses.
load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.rationale: avoid_buggy_ips does not impact the security of the service

load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.description: If true, prevent IP addresses from being automatically assigned.
load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.rationale: manual_assign does not impact the security of the service

load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.description: The name of the address pool.
load_balancer.metal_lb_config.address_po.rationale: pool does not impact the security of the service

load_balancer.vip_config.description: The VIPs used by the load balancer.

load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for the Kubernetes API of this cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for the Kubernetes API. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

load_balancer.vip_config.ingress_vip.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for ingress traffic into this cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.ingress_vip.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for ingress traffic. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

network_config.description: The VMware User Cluster network configuration.

network_config.pod_address_cidr_blocks.description:
All pods in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges.
Only a single range is supported. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.pod_address_cidr_blocks.rationale: Defines the RFC1918 IP ranges allocated to pods. The ranges are an environment-specific internal-addressing choice; a generic policy cannot constrain them without hardcoding ranges, so it is not a useful policy target.

network_config.service_address_cidr_bloc.description:
All services in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address
from these ranges. Only a single range is supported.. This field
cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.service_address_cidr_bloc.rationale: Defines the RFC1918 IP ranges allocated to services. The ranges are an environment-specific internal-addressing choice; a generic policy cannot constrain them without hardcoding ranges, so it is not a useful policy target.
